identity_admission.proof: No runtime identity, credential, or admission path is exercised or changed. Both the provisioning script and the regression module construct a minimal child environment explicitly (PATH, HOME, LANG only) and never inherit the parent process environment, so no ambient credential can reach a child.

publish_cut.reason: No hosted surface is affected. The distribution is named pantheon-repo and is never published to an index; it exists only to provision sys.path for a local checkout.

pre_deploy.reason: No hosted or deployed surface is exercised or changed. The only executed surfaces are local test runners, pip installing into throwaway environments under the scratch directory, and child interpreters spawned with an explicitly constructed minimal environment.

proof: The duplicate hazard for a packaging change is two distinct module objects for the same source file, or one checkout's packages shadowing another's. TestInstalledDistributionIsCanonical::test_module_identity_is_canonical_and_unduplicated asserts that services.telemetry.capture resolves to this checkout's capture.py, that sys.modules holds the same object, and that no bare 'capture' or 'feedback_adapter' alias is registered.

TestInstalledDistributionIsCanonical::test_repository_root_is_not_placed_on_sys_path asserts the distribution never puts the repository root on sys.path, which is what would otherwise let root-level modules load a second time under different names.

verify_checkout_binding runs on every provisioning invocation and fails closed when any exported name resolves outside the requested checkout, so the cross-worktree duplicate-identity case is detected rather than silently accepted. validation.commands[12] exercises that failure.
Provisioning is idempotent: ensure_venv reuses an existing environment and rewrites the inheritance .pth, and a second run of validation.commands[9] gives the same verification output.

The defect being closed: services is a top-level name, so with the repository neither on the working directory nor on PYTHONPATH, 'python -m unittest services.telemetry.test_capture' and 'python <abs>/test_capture.py' failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'services' before the module body ever ran. validation.commands[8] reproduces exactly that failure on an unprovisioned interpreter as the control for the passes in commands[5] and [6].

Degraded provisioning is stated rather than assumed. --check-only on an unprovisioned environment exits 1 (commands[10]); --mode current on the shared system interpreter is refused (commands[11]); a distribution bound to a different checkout is reported as a collision (commands[12]). None of the three degrades to a warning.

The editable install tries --no-build-isolation first so provisioning works with no package-index access, and falls back to an isolated build only if that fails. The CI rehearsal in commands[9] records which strategy was used ('no-build-isolation').

provisioned_interpreter() in the regression module raises AssertionError rather than skipTest when provisioning fails, so an environment where AC2 cannot be proven reads as a failure. The 20-passed / 0-skipped result in commands[2] shows no assertion was reached by the skip path.

Not a request-serving surface. The correlation this task must preserve is between the suite total and the tests that actually executed. Baseline 296 passed / 1 skipped at dev 643181a06, post-change 301 passed / 1 skipped at head c72842d9d: exactly +5, matching the 15 -> 20 growth of the one changed telemetry module. No test was lost, converted to a skip, or silently stopped running.

Each AC2 mode reports its own count and each is pinned at 75 (35 from test_capture plus 40 from test_feedback_adapter), so a mode that starts collecting fewer tests fails rather than passing with a smaller suite.
The four modes are recorded separately in validation.commands[4] through [7] with their observed counts, not aggregated into a single claim.

Provisioning is re-runnable: a second invocation reuses the existing .venv-pantheon, reinstalls the editable distribution, rewrites the inheritance .pth, and re-verifies. Nothing accumulates in the checkout.

Recovery from a wrong provision is a plain re-run: because the mapping is absolute and verification compares it against the requested checkout, a stale binding is reported (commands[12]) and corrected by provisioning again.

The provisioned environment is disposable by construction. Deleting .venv-pantheon returns the checkout to its unprovisioned state, and --check-only then reports it (commands[10]). No repository file records provisioning state.

Rollback is reverting the PR. The distribution has no installed footprint inside the repository: the editable install writes a .pth and a finder module into the target environment's site-packages only, and git status stayed clean across every install performed during validation (commands[18]).
Reverting restores the previous behaviour exactly: AC2 modes M1 and M4 keep passing on a bare checkout (they never needed packaging), and M2 and M3 return to the recorded gap.
No live supervisor, service, or deployment state is mutated, so there is nothing to compensate outside the git revert.
